title: Google Launches Dreambeans in India, Its First Market Outside US
excerpt: The Google Labs experiment turns connected Calendar, Gmail, Photos, Search and YouTube activity into personalised illustrated stories, now in English and 13 Indian languages for users aged 18 and over.
body:
• Google has launched Dreambeans, its experimental Google Labs app that turns a user's connected Google activity into personalised illustrated stories, in India — its first market outside the United States.
  • The app is available on Android and iOS for users aged 18 and over, in English and 13 Indian languages including Hindi, Punjabi, Tamil, Telugu and Bengali.
  • It draws only on services a user chooses to connect — Calendar, Gemini, Gmail, Photos, Search and YouTube — and is limited to personal Gmail accounts, not enterprise accounts.
  • US traction has been modest so far: Sensor Tower estimates shared with TechCrunch put downloads at nearly 55,000 since June, falling about 84 percent month over month to roughly 5,500 in October.

Google has launched Dreambeans in India, making the country the first market outside the United States for its experimental AI app, YourStory and TechCrunch reported. Dreambeans, developed by Google Labs, turns a user's digital activity into personalised, illustrated stories about their interests and everyday life — without the user entering a prompt.

What Dreambeans actually does

Introduced in June, the app uses Google's Personal Intelligence technology to draw on connected Google services — Calendar, Gemini, Gmail, Photos, Search and YouTube — and proactively generate a daily collection of illustrated stories, TechCrunch reported. Google recently added a feature using its Veo video-generation model to animate images in select stories. In Google's own description, quoted by YourStory from its blog post, a story "could be everything from places to explore, new arts & crafts, or a reminder of upcoming local events," and users can dive deeper into a story, bookmark it or share it. Google's Dreambeans announcement describes the same model: personalised topics distilled from the Google apps a user selects.

"This could be everything from places to explore, new arts & crafts, or a reminder of upcoming local events. You can dive deeper into any story to learn more, bookmark for later, or easily share with others to spark inspiration."

— Google, in its Dreambeans blog post, quoted by YourStory

Why India, and in what form

The app is available on Android and iOS for users above 18, YourStory reported, across 14 languages in total — English plus 13 Indian languages including Hindi, Bengali, Telugu, Marathi, Tamil, Urdu, Gujarati, Kannada, Punjabi, Assamese and Nepali. Google said it chose India as the first international market because of strong interest from Indian users seeking access and the widespread use of its services in the country; India stood out for its high overlap of users across Gemini, Gmail and Google Photos, product manager Gozde Oznur said at a press briefing reported by TechCrunch. The launch comes less than two months after Google opened the app to all eligible US users aged 18 and older.

There is a language limit that matters in India specifically. Users can select only one language at a time for their generated stories; the app can draw on information written in multiple languages across connected services, but it cannot currently generate stories that mix languages, Oznur said — a constraint in a market where many people switch between, for example, Hindi and English.

The privacy terms

Because Dreambeans reads across a user's accounts, its controls are part of the product. Users can choose which Google services to connect and disconnect them at any time, and can delete their Dreambeans data from within the app; information deleted from an underlying connected service is also removed from Dreambeans' personalisation system, Oznur said, according to TechCrunch. Users can tell the app to avoid certain subjects, and generated stories are visible only to the account holder. The app is available only to personal Gmail account holders, not enterprise users. YourStory added that a thumbs-down button flags irrelevant or wrong content, and data can be deleted anytime from settings.

What happens next

Dreambeans arrives in India with modest US numbers behind it: nearly 55,000 US downloads since June by Sensor Tower estimates shared with TechCrunch, about 63 percent of them in September when access widened, then a fall of about 84 percent to roughly 5,500 in October. Oznur told reporters Google is exploring ways to make Dreambeans more actionable — moving beyond stories and recommendations to help users act on its suggestions — but that is an exploratory direction, not an announced feature of the India release. For Indian users aged 18 and over with a personal Gmail account, the app is available now on both mobile platforms.
